title: Proverbs Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 16.

questions.question: What is said to be from the LORD in Proverbs 16:1?
options: The preparations of the heart and the answer of the tongue
questions.correctAnswer: The preparations of the heart and the answer of the tongue
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:1 states that the preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the LORD.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 16:2, what does the LORD weigh?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:2 indicates that all the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes, but the LORD weigheth the spirits.

questions.question: What should one commit to the LORD according to Proverbs 16:3?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:3 advises to commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD hath made all things for Himself, including the wicked.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:4 states that the LORD hath made all things for Himself, even the wicked for the day of evil.

questions.question: What is considered an abomination to the LORD according to Proverbs 16:5?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:5 declares that every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Mercy and truth are said to purge iniquity in Proverbs 16:6.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:6 states that by mercy and truth iniquity is purged.

questions.question: What happens when a man's ways please the LORD according to Proverbs 16:7?
options: He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him
questions.correctAnswer: He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:7 says that when a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 16:8, what is better than great revenues?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:8 emphasizes that better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 16:9 states that a man's heart deviseth his way, but the LORD directeth his steps.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:9 confirms that a man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.

questions.question: What is found in the lips of a king as stated in Proverbs 16:10?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:10 specifies that a divine sentence is in the lips of the king.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:11 say are the LORD'S?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:11 states that a just weight and balance are the LORD'S: all the weights of the bag are his work.

questions.question: In Proverbs 16, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Commit thy works unto the LORD
The preparations of the heart in man are from the LORD
A man's heart deviseth his way
Better is a little with righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: The preparations of the heart in man are from the LORD
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:1 is the first instruction in the chapter, stating that the preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the LORD.

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What is said to be an abomination to kings according to Proverbs 16?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:12 states that 'It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness: for the throne is established by righteousness.' This shows that kings value righteousness and detest wickedness.

questions.question: What type of lips are a delight to kings as mentioned in Proverbs 16?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:13 indicates that 'Righteous lips are the delight of kings; and they love him that speaketh right.' This emphasizes the importance of speaking truthfully and righteously.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 16:14, how is the wrath of a king described?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:14 states, 'The wrath of a king is as messengers of death: but a wise man will pacify it.' This illustrates the seriousness of a king's anger.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:16 compare the value of wisdom to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:16 says, 'How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! and to get understanding rather to be chosen than silver!' This highlights that wisdom is of greater value than material wealth.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:18 say precedes destruction?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:18 states, 'Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.' This warns against the dangers of pride.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 16:20, who is happy?
options: He that trusts in the LORD
He that is wise in his own eyes
questions.correctAnswer: He that trusts in the LORD
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:20 states, 'He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the LORD, happy is he.' This emphasizes the joy that comes from trusting in God.

questions.question: What is said to be the preservation of one's soul in Proverbs 16:17?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:17 states, 'The highway of the upright is to depart from evil: he that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.' This teaches that living righteously preserves one's life.

questions.question: True or False: Kings prefer deceitful speech according to Proverbs 16:13.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:13 states that 'Righteous lips are the delight of kings.' This implies that kings prefer truthful and righteous speech, making the statement false.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 16:30 suggests that a wise person devises good things.
questions.explanation: While this specific verse is not quoted, the surrounding context supports wisdom leading to good outcomes. Therefore, the statement is true.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:25 warn about the ways that seem right to a man?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:25 states, 'There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.' This warns that appearances can be misleading.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:21 say about the wise in heart?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:21 states, 'The wise in heart shall be called prudent: and the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.' This emphasizes that wisdom is recognized by discernment.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 16:22 compare understanding and the instruction of fools?
options: Understanding is life, but fools' instruction is folly
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding is life, but fools' instruction is folly
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:22 states, 'Understanding is a wellspring of life unto him that hath it: but the instruction of fools is folly.' This contrasts true understanding with foolishness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Proverbs 16:32, being slow to anger is better than being mighty.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:32 states, 'He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.' This indicates that self-control is more valuable than physical strength.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 16.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:3 suggest about committing one's works?
options: They will be established by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They will be established by the LORD
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:3 states, 'Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established', indicating that committing works to God leads to the establishment of one's thoughts.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 16:8, which is deemed better?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:8 states, 'Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right', emphasizing the value of righteousness over material gain.

questions.question: Which theme from Proverbs 16:25 is echoed in Matthew 7:13-14?
options: The way that seems right leading to death
questions.correctAnswer: The way that seems right leading to death
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:25 states, 'There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death', which is echoed in Matthew 7:13-14 about the narrow way leading to life.

questions.question: In Proverbs 16:32, who is considered better than the mighty?
options: The one who is slow to anger
questions.correctAnswer: The one who is slow to anger
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:32 states, 'He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty', highlighting the virtue of self-control over brute strength.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Proverbs 16:18, which discusses pride and destruction?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:18 employs parallelism, contrasting the concepts of pride leading to destruction and a haughty spirit preceding a fall.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:20 say about those who handle matters wisely?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:20 states, 'He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good', emphasizing the positive outcomes of wisdom in decision-making.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 16:22, what is understanding compared to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:22 states, 'Understanding is a wellspring of life unto him that hath it', highlighting the nourishing and sustaining nature of true understanding.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 16:31 states that a hoary head is a crown of glory when found in the way of righteousness.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:31 states, 'The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness', affirming the value of wisdom gained through age.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:24 say pleasant words are like?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:24 states, 'Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones', illustrating the sweetness and beneficial nature of kind words.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 16:30 indicates that a man who devises froward things brings about good.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:30 suggests that a man who devises froward things brings about evil, showing the negative consequences of such actions.

questions.question: In Proverbs 16:27, how is an ungodly man described?
options: As one who diggeth up evil
questions.correctAnswer: As one who diggeth up evil
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:27 describes an ungodly man as one who 'diggeth up evil', indicating his propensity for negativity and strife.

questions.question: What key Hebrew word in Proverbs 16:20 denotes wisdom and understanding, often translated as 'wise'?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Chokmah', found in Proverbs 16:20, denotes wisdom and insight, emphasizing the importance of wise handling of matters.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 16:29, what does a violent man do?
options: Entices his neighbor into the way that is not good
questions.correctAnswer: Entices his neighbor into the way that is not good
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:29 states, 'A violent man enticeth his neighbour, and leadeth him into the way that is not good', warning against the influence of violent individuals.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:33 imply about the lot cast into the lap?
options: The whole disposing thereof is of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The whole disposing thereof is of the LORD
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:33 states, 'The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of the LORD', emphasizing divine sovereignty over chance.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:1 teach about the source of human thoughts and responses?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:1 states that the preparations of the heart in man and the answer of the tongue is from the LORD, indicating that both thoughts and speech are ultimately guided by divine influence.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 16:2, whose assessment of a man's ways is ultimately correct?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:2 declares that while a man may see his own ways as clean, it is the LORD who weighs the spirits, highlighting divine judgment over human perception.

questions.question: What is the relationship between committing works to the LORD and establishing thoughts, as per Proverbs 16:3?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:3 teaches that when one commits their works to the LORD, their thoughts shall be established, indicating a direct link between action and mental clarity.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated in Proverbs 16:4 regarding His creation?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:4 states that the LORD has made all things for Himself, showcasing His sovereignty in creation and purpose.

questions.question: What warning does Proverbs 16:5 give about pride?
options: It is an abomination to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: It is an abomination to the LORD
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:5 tells us that every proud heart is an abomination to the LORD, emphasizing the seriousness of pride in the sight of God.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 16:6 describe the way iniquity is purged?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:6 states that iniquity is purged by mercy and truth, indicating that divine attributes are essential for forgiveness and cleansing.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:8 imply about wealth obtained without righteousness?
options: It is favored by the LORD
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:8 asserts that better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right, indicating the futility of wealth gained immorally.

questions.question: What insight does Proverbs 16:19 provide about humility?
options: It is less valuable than pride
It is better than sharing spoils with the proud
questions.correctAnswer: It is better than sharing spoils with the proud
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:19 highlights that it is better to be of a humble spirit with the lowly than to divide the spoils with the proud, emphasizing the value of humility over pride.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:24 say about the nature of pleasant words?
options: They are sweet to the soul
questions.correctAnswer: They are sweet to the soul
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:24 describes pleasant words as sweet to the soul and health to the bones, underscoring the positive impact of kind speech.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 16:27, what characterizes an ungodly man?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:27 characterizes an ungodly man as one who digs up evil, emphasizing his inclination towards wrongdoing and malice.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 16:30 illustrate the behavior of a froward man?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:30 illustrates that a froward man shuts his eyes to devise froward things, indicating his scheming nature focused on evil.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 16:32 teach about self-control?
options: It is less important than physical strength
It is a sign of weakness
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:32 states that he who is slow to anger is better than the mighty, emphasizing the value of self-control over brute strength.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Proverbs 16:18 and 16:19 convey about pride?
options: Pride precedes destruction, humility brings safety
questions.correctAnswer: Pride precedes destruction, humility brings safety
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:18 warns that pride goes before destruction, while 16:19 highlights that humility is better than sharing with the proud, together teaching that pride leads to downfall while humility offers protection.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not care about our thoughts and actions. What does Proverbs 16:1-3 actually teach?
options: God is indifferent to human affairs
God actively influences our hearts and responses
God only cares about our actions
questions.correctAnswer: God actively influences our hearts and responses
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:1-3 reveals that both the preparations of the heart and the answers of the tongue come from the LORD, emphasizing His active role in guiding human thoughts and actions.

questions.question: What synthesis of teaching do Proverbs 16:6 and 16:17 convey about righteousness and evil?
options: Righteousness brings peace and departs from evil
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness brings peace and departs from evil
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:6 states that mercy and truth purges iniquity, while 16:17 notes that the highway of the upright departs from evil, together illustrating that righteousness leads to peace and a departure from wrongdoing.
